e1.name: Shell-and-Tube Heat Exchanger
e1.summary: Vary flow rates and inlet temperatures across a two-pass exchanger, then derive the effectiveness–NTU relationship from your own readings.
e1.desc: Learners set the hot and cold flow rates and inlet temperatures on a two-pass shell-and-tube exchanger, read the four terminal temperatures and work out the heat duty. From several runs they derive effectiveness against NTU and compare it with the textbook curve.
e1.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop

AR.label: Shell-and-Tube — AR build 1.0
AR.device: A supported phone or tablet with a rear camera
AR.install: Install the build named above and open “Heat Exchanger Lab”.

VR.label: Shell-and-Tube — VR build 1.0
VR.device: Standalone VR headset and about 2 × 2 m of clear floor
VR.install: Install the build named above on the headset and open “Heat Exchanger Lab”.

outcomes: Calculate heat duty and effectiveness from measured terminal temperatures.
Relate effectiveness to NTU for a two-pass exchanger.
Explain how the flow rates change the overall heat transfer coefficient.

hist.note: First publication by the Content Manager.

e2.name: Fin-Tube Bundle
e2.summary: Introduce progressive fouling on the tube side and measure its effect on the overall heat transfer coefficient.
e2.desc: Learners blow air across a finned tube bundle, add fouling to the tube side in steps and record the inlet and outlet temperatures at each step. They work out the overall heat transfer coefficient and the fouling resistance, and explain the trend.
e2.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop

VR.label: Fin-Tube Bundle — VR build 1.0
VR.device: Standalone VR headset and about 2 × 2 m of clear floor
VR.install: Install the build named above on the headset and open “Fin-Tube Lab”.

outcomes: Work out the overall heat transfer coefficient from measured temperatures.
Estimate the fouling resistance from the drop in performance.

hist.note: First publication by the Content Manager, from SUB-0052.

e3.name: Composite Wall Conduction
e3.summary: Build a layered wall, measure the temperature profile and separate the contribution of each material.
e3.desc: Learners assemble a wall from layers of different materials, hold a fixed temperature difference across it and read the temperature at each interface. From the measured profile they work out the thermal resistance of each layer.
e3.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop

AR.label: Composite Wall Conduction — AR build 1.0
AR.device: A supported phone or tablet with a rear camera
AR.install: Install the build named above and open “Wall Lab”.

outcomes: Work out the thermal resistance of each layer from a measured temperature profile.
Explain why the largest temperature drop falls across the most resistive layer.

hist.note: First publication by the Content Manager.

e4.name: CNC Turning Centre
e4.summary: Set up a turning operation, choose speeds and feeds, and see how they change cutting force and surface finish.
e4.desc: Learners load a part program on a CNC turning centre, choose the cutting speed, feed and depth of cut, and run the cycle. They read the cutting force and the surface finish for each setting and choose the setting that meets the drawing.
e4.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop

AR.label: CNC Turning Centre — AR build 1.0
AR.device: A supported phone or tablet with a rear camera
AR.install: Install the build named above and open “Turning Lab”.

VR.label: CNC Turning Centre — VR build 1.0
VR.device: Standalone VR headset and about 2 × 2 m of clear floor
VR.install: Install the build named above on the headset and open “Turning Lab”.

MR.label: CNC Turning Centre — MR build 1.0
MR.device: A supported mixed-reality headset and a clear table or floor area
MR.install: Install the build named above on the headset and open “Turning Lab”.

outcomes: Choose cutting speed, feed and depth of cut for a given material.
Relate the chosen settings to cutting force and surface finish.

hist.note: First publication by the Content Manager.

e5.name: Investment Casting
e5.summary: Follow a part from wax pattern to finished casting and find where its defects come from.
e5.desc: Learners make the wax pattern, build the ceramic shell, choose the pouring temperature and inspect the cast part. They trace each defect they find back to the step that caused it.
e5.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop
outcomes: Put the investment casting steps in order and say what each one does.
Trace a casting defect back to the step that caused it.

hist.note: First publication by the Content Manager.

e6.name: Induction Motor Loading
e6.summary: Load a three-phase induction motor step by step and see how its speed, current and efficiency change.
e6.desc: Learners load a three-phase induction motor on a brake dynamometer in steps from no load to full load. At each step they record the speed, line current, input power and torque, then plot efficiency and power factor against load.
e6.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop

VR.label: Induction Motor Loading — VR build 1.0
VR.device: Standalone VR headset and about 2 × 2 m of clear floor
VR.install: Install the build named above on the headset and open “Motor Lab”.

MR.label: Induction Motor Loading — MR build 1.0
MR.device: A supported mixed-reality headset and a clear table or floor area
MR.install: Install the build named above on the headset and open “Motor Lab”.

outcomes: Measure speed, current, input power and torque across the load range.
Plot efficiency and power factor against load and explain their shape.

hist.note: First publication by the Content Manager.

e7.name: Synchronous Generator
e7.summary: Bring a synchronous generator onto the grid and see how its excitation changes the reactive power.
e7.desc: Learners run a synchronous generator up to speed, match its voltage, frequency and phase to the grid, and close the breaker. They then change the excitation and watch the reactive power and the power factor change.
e7.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop

VR.label: Synchronous Generator — VR build 1.0
VR.device: Standalone VR headset and about 2 × 2 m of clear floor
VR.install: Install the build named above on the headset and open “Generator Lab”.

outcomes: Synchronise a generator with the grid in the right order.
Explain how excitation controls the reactive power.

hist.note: First publication by the Content Manager.

e8.name: Transformer Tests
e8.summary: Run the open-circuit and short-circuit tests and build the equivalent circuit of a transformer.
e8.desc: Learners run the open-circuit and short-circuit tests on a single-phase transformer, record voltage, current and power, and work out the equivalent-circuit parameters. They use them to predict efficiency and voltage regulation at a chosen load.
e8.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop
outcomes: Work out equivalent-circuit parameters from open- and short-circuit test readings.
Predict efficiency and voltage regulation at a given load.

hist.note: First publication by the Content Manager.

e9.name: Buck Converter Ripple
e9.summary: Change the inductor, capacitor and switching frequency of a buck converter and measure the output ripple.
e9.desc: Learners run a buck converter at a fixed duty cycle, then change the inductor, the output capacitor and the switching frequency one at a time. They measure the output voltage ripple and compare it with the predicted value.
e9.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop

AR.label: Buck Converter Ripple — AR build 1.0
AR.device: A supported phone or tablet with a rear camera
AR.install: Install the build named above and open “Converter Lab”.

outcomes: Predict the output voltage ripple from the inductor, capacitor and switching frequency.
Explain the trade-off between ripple and component size.

hist.note: First publication by the Content Manager.

e10.name: Distillation Column
e10.summary: Bring a binary column from cold start to steady state, tuning reflux ratio against overhead purity under realistic lag.
e10.desc: Learners start a binary column from cold and bring it to steady state. They then change the reflux ratio and watch the overhead purity respond with realistic lag. Lowering the reflux ratio raises the overhead purity, at the cost of more reboiler heat.
e10.browser: A current browser on a laptop or desktop

VR.label: Distillation Column — VR build 1.2
VR.device: Standalone VR headset and about 2 × 2 m of clear floor
VR.install: Install the build named above and open “Column Lab”.

outcomes: Bring a column to steady state from cold start
Tune reflux ratio against an overhead purity target

hist.note: Correction UPD-0002 — released by the Super Admin.
First publication by the Content Manager.

e11.name: Boiler Drum Level
e11.summary: Hold a boiler drum level steady through load changes and see why single-element control struggles.
e11.desc: Learners control the water level in a boiler drum while the steam demand changes. They compare single-element and three-element control and see how swell and shrink mislead a simple level controller.
e11.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop

VR.label: Boiler Drum Level — VR build 2.0
VR.device: Standalone VR headset and about 2 × 2 m of clear floor
VR.install: Install the build named above on the headset and open “Boiler Lab”.

outcomes: Explain swell and shrink and how they mislead a level controller.
Compare single-element and three-element drum level control.

e12.name: Orifice Plate Metering
e12.summary: Measure flow with an orifice plate and find its discharge coefficient from your own readings.
e12.desc: Learners read the pressure drop across an orifice plate, taken at flange tappings, at several flow rates and work out the flow from it. Comparing with a reference meter, they find the discharge coefficient of the plate and where it stops being constant.
e12.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop

AR.label: Orifice Plate Metering — AR build 1.0
AR.device: A supported phone or tablet with a rear camera
AR.install: Install the build named above and open “Flow Lab”.

outcomes: Work out the flow from the pressure drop across an orifice plate.
Find the discharge coefficient and the range where it holds.

hist.note: Correction UPD-0003 — released by the Super Admin.
First publication by the Content Manager.

SUB-0077.name: Conduction Through a Composite Wall
SUB-0077.summary: Measure the temperature profile across a three-layer wall and compare it with the series-resistance model.
SUB-0077.desc: Learners build a wall from three layers — brick, insulation and plaster — set the hot-side and cold-side temperatures, and read the temperature at each interface. They compare the measured profile and heat flux with the series thermal-resistance model and explain where the two differ.
SUB-0077.browser: A current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop, with a keyboard and mouse

VR.label: Composite Wall — VR build 1.0
VR.device: Standalone VR headset — no PC or cable needed — and about 2 × 2 m of clear floor
VR.install: Install the build named above on the headset and open “Composite Wall Lab”. On first launch, set the play-area boundary.

outcomes: Explain conduction through layers in series using thermal resistance.
Predict interface temperatures from layer properties.
Compare measured and predicted heat flux and explain the difference.

SUB-0074.name: Transient Cooling
SUB-0074.summary: Cool a heated cylinder in still air and water, and test when the lumped-capacitance model holds.
SUB-0074.desc: Learners heat aluminium and steel cylinders, log their cooling in air and in water, and compare the curves with the lumped model using the Biot number.
SUB-0074.browser: A current browser on a laptop or desktop
outcomes: Decide when the lumped-capacitance model applies, using the Biot number.
Estimate a heat transfer coefficient from a measured cooling curve.

sh.note: Sent to the Content Manager with 2 learning outcomes. Nothing is published.

SUB-0070.name: Packed Bed Pressure Drop
SUB-0070.summary: Push air through a packed bed and compare the pressure drop you measure with the Ergun equation.
SUB-0070.desc: Learners change the air flow through beds of glass beads and Raschig rings, read the pressure drop, and fit the Ergun constants from their own data.
SUB-0070.browser: A current browser on a laptop or desktop

AR.label: Packed Bed — AR build 1.0
AR.device: Phone or tablet with a rear camera
AR.install: Install “Packed Bed AR” and point the camera at a table.

outcomes: Measure the pressure drop across a packed bed over a range of air flows.
Fit the Ergun constants from your own readings.
Explain how the packing changes the pressure drop.

sh.note: Sent to the Content Manager with 3 learning outcomes. Nothing is published.

SUB-0086.name: Flash Distillation
SUB-0086.summary: Flash a hot binary feed across a valve into a drum and find the vapour fraction from your own readings.
SUB-0086.desc: Learners set the feed temperature and the drum pressure, read the vapour and liquid flows, and compare the vapour fraction with an equilibrium calculation.
SUB-0086.browser: A current browser on a laptop or desktop
